result.keywords: This paper examines the use of satellite bathymetry, autonomous buoy arrays, and spectral signal decomposition to predict resonance patterns in shallow seabed basins. We propose a hybrid forecasting framework that combines geospatial interpolation with tidal anomaly detection to improve long-horizon marine navigation planning. Case studies from enclosed coastal lagoons demonstrate that cartographic uncertainty can be reduced by fusing multisource oceanographic observations with historical sediment-shift records. The approach is intended for environmental monitoring and maritime route advisory applications rather than robotic control or microfluidic sensing.
result.title: Nebula Cartography for Seabed Resonance Forecasting.
